key_insight: WebSwarm turns web search into a recursive tree of collaborating agents, so the system can expand both depth and coverage during inference instead of forcing one agent to do everything in a single long trajectory.
engineering_relevance: The framework is directly relevant for building scalable research assistants and search pipelines that need adaptive decomposition, evidence-grounded exploration, and efficient collaboration under context limits.
method: Dynamically instantiates agentic search nodes with a local objective plus a search mode
Each node can solve locally or delegate child nodes recursively, then pass evidence and results upward
Probes web information structure first and reuses process-level experience across homogeneous sibling nodes
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains over single-agent and multi-agent baselines on BrowseComp-Plus, WideSearch, DeepWideSearch, and GISA, with analyses across ablations, task difficulty, tool efficiency, and model generalization.
watch_item: Recursive delegation and collaboration may increase orchestration complexity and tool usage, so performance can depend on robust node control, stopping criteria, and reliable evidence propagation.
paper_title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
